literal: Even when poured and seeing it, poison having consumed they will remain composed, those who desire desirable benignity.
translation: Those who desire the highly esteemed virtue of benignity will calmly drink even poison, even when they see it being poured out for them.
modern: விரும்பத்தக்க கண்ணோட்டத்தை (நாகரிகத்தை) விரும்புகின்றவர்கள், தமக்கு நஞ்சை ஊற்றுவதைக் கண்ணால் கண்டபோதும் அதை உண்டு அமைதியாக இருப்பார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the ultimate limit of 'kaṇṇōṭtam' (benignity or consideration for others), which is here referred to as 'nākarikam' (civility or social refinement). Those who cherish this noble quality ('nākarikam vēṇṭupavar') value their relationships so highly that they would rather suffer than cause distress to others. Even if they openly see poison being served to them by someone, they will calmly drink it to avoid embarrassing or offending the host. The word 'nayattakka' emphasizes that this level of courtesy is highly desirable and worthy of praise.
